UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile within the Islamly application, storing preferences and data associated with their unique identifier from an external authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, typically provided by an external authentication system.

preferredCalculationMethod.description: The user's chosen method for calculating daily prayer times (e.g., 'MWL', 'ISNA', 'Egyptian').

madhab.description: The user's chosen juristic method for determining the Asr prayer time (e.g., 'Hanafi', 'Standard').

latitude.description: The geographical latitude of the user's location, used for prayer time calculations.

longitude.description: The geographical longitude of the user's location, used for prayer time calculations.

timeZone.description: The user's preferred or detected time zone (e.g., 'America/New_York').

preferredLanguage.description: The display name of the user's preferred translation language.

preferredLanguageId.description: The ID of the translation resource from the external API.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was last updated.

Text.title: Text
Text.description: Represents a classical Islamic text, scholarly work, Hadith collection, Quran, Seerah compilation, or Adhkar collection within the app's library.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Text entity.

title.description: The primary title of the text (e.g., 'Sahih Bukhari', 'The Holy Quran').

originalTitle.description: The original Arabic title of the text, if applicable.

author.description: The author or compiler of the text (e.g., 'Imam Bukhari').

description.description: A brief summary or introduction to the text.

language.description: The primary language of the text content (e.g., 'ar' for Arabic, 'en' for English).

publicationYear.description: The year of publication or compilation of the text.

sourceUrl.description: An optional URL pointing to the external source or origin of the text.

Chapter.title: Chapter
Chapter.description: Represents a chapter, section, or book within a larger text, providing structure to content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Chapter entity.

textId.description: Reference to the parent Text entity. (Relationship: Text 1:N Chapter)

title.description: The title of the chapter or section.

originalTitle.description: The original Arabic title of the chapter, if applicable.

order.description: The sequential order of the chapter within its parent text or collection.

description.description: A brief description or summary of the chapter.

Passage.title: Passage
Passage.description: Represents a granular unit of content, such as a Quranic verse, Hadith, Dua, or a paragraph from a scholarly text.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Passage entity.

textId.description: Reference to the parent Text entity. (Relationship: Text 1:N Passage)

chapterId.description: Optional reference to the parent Chapter entity, if the passage belongs to a specific chapter. (Relationship: Chapter 1:N Passage)

type.description: The specific type of content represented by this passage (e.g., 'Verse', 'Hadith', 'Dua', 'Paragraph', 'ScholarlyPassage').

contentArabic.description: The original text content in Arabic.

contentTranslation.description: The English translation of the content.

contentTransliteration.description: The transliteration of the Arabic content, useful for non-Arabic speakers.

commentary.description: Associated tafsir, explanation, or commentary for the passage.

sourceReference.description: A specific reference string within the original source (e.g., 'Surah 2: Ayat 255', 'Bukhari 1:1', 'Hisnul Muslim No. 12').

order.description: The sequential order of the passage within its parent chapter or text.

pageNumber.description: The page number within the physical source text, if applicable.

Bookmark.title: Bookmark
Bookmark.description: Allows users to bookmark favorite texts, chapters, or specific passages for quick reference.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Bookmark entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created the bookmark. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Bookmark)

targetType.description: Specifies the type of content being bookmarked ('Text', 'Chapter', or 'Passage').

targetId.description: The ID of the content entity being bookmarked (Text.id, Chapter.id, or Passage.id, depending on targetType).

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the bookmark was created.

Note.title: Note
Note.description: Stores personal notes added by users to specific passages within the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Note entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who created the note. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Note)

passageId.description: Reference to the Passage entity to which the note is attached. (Relationship: Passage 1:N Note)

content.description: The actual text content of the personal note.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the note was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the note was last updated.

Quiz.title: Quiz
Quiz.description: Defines an Islamic quiz with its title, description, topic, and difficulty.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Quiz entity.

description.description: A brief description of the quiz's content or focus.

topic.description: The primary topic covered by the quiz (e.g., 'Quran', 'Hadith', 'Seerah', 'Fiqh').

difficulty.description: The difficulty level of the quiz ('Beginner', 'Intermediate', 'Advanced').

Question.title: Question
Question.description: Represents an individual question belonging to a quiz, including its text, type, options, and correct answer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Question entity.

quizId.description: Reference to the parent Quiz entity. (Relationship: Quiz 1:N Question)

questionText.description: The full text of the question.

options.description: An array of possible answer options for multiple-choice questions.

correctAnswer.description: The correct answer to the question.

explanation.description: An explanation or rationale for the correct answer.

QuizAttempt.title: QuizAttempt
QuizAttempt.description: Records a user's attempt at a specific quiz, including start/end times and overall score.

id.description: Unique identifier for the QuizAttempt entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who made the attempt. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N QuizAttempt)

quizId.description: Reference to the Quiz that was attempted. (Relationship: Quiz 1:N QuizAttempt)

startTime.description: Timestamp indicating when the quiz attempt started.

endTime.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the quiz attempt ended.

score.description: The score obtained by the user in this quiz attempt (e.g., percentage or raw score).

isCompleted.description: A boolean indicating whether the quiz attempt was fully completed.

QuizAnswer.title: QuizAnswer
QuizAnswer.description: Stores a user's specific answer to a question within a quiz attempt.

id.description: Unique identifier for the QuizAnswer entity.

quizAttemptId.description: Reference to the parent QuizAttempt. (Relationship: QuizAttempt 1:N QuizAnswer)

questionId.description: Reference to the Question being answered. (Relationship: Question 1:N QuizAnswer)

userAnswer.description: The answer provided by the user for this question.

isCorrect.description: Indicates whether the user's provided answer was correct.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. Access is restricted to the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`). Includes denormalized 'id' (which is the userId) for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, corresponding to `request.auth.uid`.

definition.description: Contains a global, public collection of Islamic texts. Authenticated users have read-only access. No specific owner, accessible by all users.

Subcollection of chapters belonging to a specific text. Authenticated users have read-only access. Logically nested for organization, sharing the parent text's public access posture. The 'textId' is included in the document for query consistency.

Subcollection of passages belonging to a specific text. Authenticated users have read-only access. Allows passages to exist directly under a text, with an optional 'chapterId' field for further categorization.
Stores user-specific bookmarks. Access is restricted to the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`). Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence and query efficiency.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this bookmark.

params.name: bookmarkId
params.description: The unique identifier of the bookmark.

definition.description: Stores user-specific personal notes. Access is restricted to the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`). Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence and query efficiency.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this note.

params.name: noteId
params.description: The unique identifier of the note.

definition.description: Contains a global, public collection of Islamic quizzes. Authenticated users have read-only access. No specific owner, accessible by all users.
Subcollection of questions belonging to a specific quiz. Authenticated users have read-only access. Logically nested for organization, sharing the parent quiz's public access posture.
Records user-specific attempts at quizzes. Access is restricted to the owner (`request.auth.uid == userId`). Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence and query efficiency.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who made this quiz attempt.

params.name: quizAttemptId
params.description: The unique identifier of the quiz attempt.

definition.description: Stores user's answers to questions within a specific quiz attempt. Access is restricted to the owner of the parent quiz attempt (`request.auth.uid == userId`). The 'userId' is implicitly available via the parent path for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the parent quiz attempt.

params.name: quizAttemptId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent quiz attempt.

params.name: quizAnswerId
params.description: The unique identifier of the quiz answer.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for Islamly prioritizes clear authorization, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** Authorization is primarily achieved through path-based ownership for user-specific data and universal read access for public content, eliminating the need for `get()` calls in security rules. For example, user profiles, bookmarks, notes, quiz attempts, and quiz answers are all nested directly under `/users/{userId}/...`. The `userId` in the path (e.g., `{userId}`) directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`, making authorization checks atomic and independent of parent document fetches. For entities like `Bookmark`, `Note`, and `QuizAttempt`, the `userId` field is also explicitly included in the document schema, serving as a denormalized authorization context that reinforces ownership and enables direct queries, even though the path itself is sufficient for rules. Public content (Texts, Chapters, Passages, Quizzes, Questions) is placed in root-level or nested root-level collections, granting authenticated users read-only access without any complex authorization dependencies.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This structure inherently supports Query-Able Paths (QAPs). For user-owned data, `list` operations are implicitly scoped by the `/users/{userId}/` path segment, meaning a user can only list their own bookmarks, notes, quiz attempts, and quiz answers. For public content, `list` operations on collections like `/texts` or `/quizzes` are permitted for all authenticated users, allowing efficient browsing and searching of the library without requiring complex rule-based filtering. The structural segregation ensures that public data and private user data have distinct, simple security postures, making rules straightforward and performant.
